POST-ELECTIONS WRAP

By: Ntokozo Miya | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The votes have been cast and counted, will South Africa become “Coalition Country”?

Unique Selling Point:
A band of renowned political analysts talk us through the likehood of coalitions and parties who have emerged as kingmakers, while the public reflects on their votes and what influenced their decisions when putting the 'X' on the ballot paper and their expectations from the parties they chose.

Summary:
With the ANC having relied on coalitions in recent elections, we discuss the party's performance in these elections with a focus on the results that would have been tallied in the days after voting.
The voting public, who voiced confusion and dissatisfaction with their party choices in last week's insert, get to reflect on what influenced their final decision when casting their votes.

Further information:
We also recap some of the controversies that unfolded during the election period e.g. reports of discoveries of suspicious ballot boxes and allegations of political party misconduct.
The CB team has agreed to voting day video submissions where possible. The social media team will encourage voters to do the same, which will make the insert very colorful.

Press Release:



Elections 2019
Battered and bruised, the campaign trail took its toll on political parties that traversed the country trying to move the needle during this year’s national elections. By Tuesday the electorate still seemed confused and millions of votes were up for grabs. By Thursday, the die was cast. But in the final tally, will South Africans’ votes result in more than coalitions and compromises? Carte Blanche analyses the country’s sixth democratic elections.
Producer: Ntokozo Miya
Presenter: Macfarlane Moleli


Script:


POST-ELECTIONS SKELETON – FINAL WITH PROMOS
AUDIO
CYRIL RAMAPHOSA – ANC – (party videos project)

00:13:50:23 – ... South Africans deserve the best of any service that we can give.
JULIUS MALEMA - EFF – (party videos project)


00:14:42:10 – (Malema VO) Our fight for the land is about giving dignity to black people. … (Malema on-camera) Vote for the only party willing to make a difference.
MMUSI MAIMANE – DA - (party videos project)

00:12:49:02 – … Fellow South Africans, I will have zero tolerance for corruption. This is the only way we’ll build our country.
LINK – Having heard more promises of improved service delivery, job creation and an end to corruption, South Africans took to the polls to choose their leadership for the next five years.
SELLO - (voxie project)

00:00:05:04 – The main reason why I decided to vote today – first thing is clamping down on crime in our country and then secondly, to get rid of corruption within our government.
CHARLIE - (voxie project)

00:02:10:03 – We’ve got to get rid of the poverty, for starters, and then unemployment – that’s also got to go.
INNOCENTIA - (voxie project)

00:00:39:07 – ... People need to get jobs so that they can maintain and support themselves rather than handouts from the government.
JACKIE - (voxie project)

00:01:08:16 – I brought my son with so it’s to show him that even a small little cross on a piece of paper will make all the difference in the world.
VO – While some parties managed to attract youngsters, for others, the youth vote was still out of reach, says columnist, Peter Bruce.
PETER BRUCE – COLUMNIST

Young people are cynical about politics. They are woke and they do know what’s going on but they are also unable to join up the act of voting to the outcome of a different way of dealing with the problem that they live with.
VO – Election day excitement turned to concern when voters noticed that the ink stain on their thumbs faded shortly after they’d left the polling station.

It is believed that fraudsters were able to vote at multiple stations after removing the ink stain with ease.

The IEC said there were many ways to process voters to ensure that they only voted once and it would have been difficult for criminals to bypass all of them.
LINK – Rapidly fading ink and double-voting were not the only issues that threatened to put a damper on this year’s elections.
VO – In Limpopo, an IEC official was suspended following the discovery of ballot boxes on the roadside.

Service delivery protests interrupted voting in KZN, Eastern Cape and Western Cape.

Videos showing mishandling of ballot boxes trended on social media, including this one posted by UDM leader Bantu Holomisa. The clip shows two women allegedly “depositing ballot papers long after party agents had left”.
UPSOUND - (links, interviews and other project)

Man behind camera - “So you are sealing the boxes here at the IEC and not at the centre?”
Lady with ballot box - “Please don’t take a video of me.”
Man behind camera - “I can’t not take a video because what you are doing is not ri ght.”
VO – Despite a number of potentially damaging incidents, the IEC says the final election outcome is a true reflection of voter choices.
GLEN MASHININI - IEC

The following parties will represented in the 6th national assembly...the Economic Freedom Fighters with 44 seats, the official opposition in the sixth parliament will be the Democratic Alliance with 84 seats. Finally, for sixth time in 26 years, the majority party in the national assembly of South Africa is the African National Congress. The Electoral Commisssion of South Africa wishes now to declare the elections to be free and fair.
VO – The national results saw the ruling party lose a huge chunk of its supporters. Political analyst Thabo Shole Mashao says scandals are to blame.
THABO SHOLE-MASHAO – POLITICAL ANALYST - (links, interviews and other project)

00:06:44:17 - ... We’ve seen the Zondo Commission. We’ve seen internal fighting. We have seen corruption allegations.
VO – The Freedom Front Plus saw huge gains at the polls and Shole-Mashao thinks the party is likely to continue to attract more supporters.
THABO SHOLE-MASHAO – POLITICAL ANALYST - (links, interviews and other project)

00:07:34:12 – The land issue will also move a number of white voters, traditionally white voters, from the DA to someone who is more clear as to what they are saying on the land issue, like the Freedom Front Plus.
VO – The DA prefers to explore a win-win situation by enforcing current land reform programs while the Freedom Front Plus is firmly against land expropriation without compensation.
PETER BRUCE – COLUMNIST

I think it basically has had more of an effect on the DA. The Freedom Front Plus has gained at the expense of the DA. You can see it is almost binary. That would have been clearly a reaction to the land expropriation without compensation debate.
VO - The EFF has much to celebrate, having increased its support base beyond the ten per cent mark.
THABO SHOLE-MASHAO – POLITICAL ANALYST - (links, interviews and other project)

00:08:13:09 – Their marketing has been spot on. ‘Land and jobs now’ - simplicity. ... They are vocal. They have media attention so they will grow.
VO – At provincial level, all were eyes on Gauteng, where the ANC was skating dangerously close to the 50 per cent mark, fueling talks of possible coalitions.

Not surprising, says Leon Schreiber, author of ‘Coalition Country’.
LEON SCHREIBER – AUTHOR – (Greg, clip 5)

We already have these minority governments in Johannesburg, Tshwane and also a coalition in Ekurhuleni, Gauteng very much is a coalition province. if you look at the fact that the ANC actually declined quite significantly on national level to well below 60% for the first time, and if you look at how tight the race was in Gauteng as well as in places like KwaZulu Natal and the Eastern Cape, you can see that the scene is being set for coalitions whenever the ANC does eventually drop below 50%.
VO – Coalitions are fragile by nature - the DA and EFF’s union in Eastern Cape’s Nelson Mandela Bay ended when the parties failed to agree on land occupation policies.
LEON SCHREIBER – AUTHOR – (Greg, clip 6)

In a multi-party coalition or minority government, it’s not a question of whether you will disagree, it’s only a question of when and how often. If you are able to establish clear mechanisms on how you are going to resolve those inevitable disputes right from the start, I think you equip yourself much better than if you wait for a dispute to arise and then scramble, trying to figure out how to actually solve it.
VO – The DA retained the Western Cape despite a drop in numbers which might have been influenced by infighting. Patricia De Lille’s newly-formed GOOD Party scooped just over 3% of the votes in the province.

In KZN, the IFP regained its status as official opposition after losing it to the DA in the 2014 elections.
THABO SHOLE-MASHAO – POLITICAL ANALYST - (links, interviews and other project)

00:05:14:08 - A lot of people were saying it’s gone, it’s dead but it’s come back, taking darth of NFP and also taking some votes from the ANC.
VO – After the election results the smaller parties detailed how they plan to improve their performance in the next elections.
POLITICAL PARTIES

GCOBANI NZONGANA – LAND PARTY

Our plan is very simple. We are starting now to work, to hit the ground, to make sure that we swell the organisation in other provinces and other regions around the Western Cape so that we know that we come up with the good number that will reflect positively in the results when they announce in the next coming 5 years.

MOSIUOA LEKOTA – COPE

We are not happy with how the elections have gone. You can see that this dual-voting, these voting stations not opening on time and all if that has cost us a lot of votes.

AUBREY MHLONGO – AIC

We will meet as a party and we will make sure that when we go to parliament, we make sure that our representatives in parliament will deliver what we promised the voters out there when we were doing the door-to-door campaign and all those things.
VO – South Africans now wait to see if their elected leaders will in fact deliver on their election promises of a better life for all.
JAMES - (voxie project)

00:01:19:07 – This country just needs to use whatever resources we have – people resources, natural resources – to actually develop to the level where we very easily can get to.
CHARLIE - (voxie project)

00:02:19:03 – Grow the country. I think that’s what we need to do – stand united, grow our country. Our country is beautiful.

PROMOS
With the elections having come and gone, we analyze the outcome, political parties plan for the work ahead while voters hope the leaders they chose will act on their promises.

We analyse the results of the recent elections while anxious South Africans wait to see if this time, politicians will deliver on their campaign promises.

Politicians spared no effort to attract voters in the recent elections, with votes having been cast and counted, we check who the winners and losers are.
